1.explanation:
• index-test.js covers the CLI’s entrypoint and confirms which messages the tool prints at startup and teardown.  
• runner-test.js exercises the runLightHouse() path where the ‘Runtime error encountered’ banner and stack traces are emitted.  
• lib/i18n/i18n-test.js, locales-test.js, and swap-locale-test.js verify the core translation factory, available locale bundles, and the ability to swap languages at runtime.  
Together these files pinpoint where the CLI output is constructed versus where translations should be applied, so you can trace why those fatal-run messages never get passed through the i18n layer.
1.bug_scenario: When invoking the Lighthouse CLI with a “–view” flag against an invalid or test URL (e.g. node lighthouse-cli www.example.com --view), the terminal emits a fatal error stack (“LHError: INVALID_URL…”) but none of the surrounding CLI messages ("Waiting for browser…", "Killing Chrome instance…", or the “Runtime error encountered” prefix) are passed through the i18n translation machinery. All of those hard-coded English strings appear untranslated, even though the codebase has a full set of locale files and swap-locale logic.
